_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 20 (Abraham, Sarah, Abimelech). Saadia-specific moves: v.1 gerar=אלכ'לוץ (the Khalus); v.3 'מלך אללה' = 'angel of God' (not God Himself appearing in a dream — anti-anthropomorphic mediation); v.4 'ארגל צאלח' = 'a righteous man' (Saadia takes גוי as 'individual', not 'nation', interpretively); v.7 'נבי וידעו לך' = 'a prophet who shall pray/call for you' (renders יתפלל as 'pray/call'); v.16 'דרהם' = 'drachma' (renders כסף = pieces of silver as Arabic dirhams).

translations.1: Then Abraham journeyed from there to the land of the qibla (the south); and he settled between Rekem (Kadesh) and al-Ghafar (Shur); and he dwelt in al-Khalus (Gerar).
translations.2: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife: 'She is my sister.' And Abimelech, king of al-Khalus (Gerar), sent and took her.
translations.3: And the angel of God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night; and he said to him: 'Behold, you are a dead man, on account of the woman whom you have taken — for she is a man's wife.'
translations.4: And Abimelech had not come near her. And he said: 'O Lord, will You slay a righteous man?
translations.5: Did he not say to me, "She is my sister" — and she too said, "He is my brother"? In the soundness of my heart and in the cleanness of my palms have I done this.'
translations.6: And the angel of God said to him in the dream: 'I, too, know that you did this in the soundness of your heart; therefore I held you back, by making it known to you, from sinning against Me; and therefore I did not let you draw near her.
translations.7: Now restore the man's wife — for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you shall live. And if you do not restore her, know that you shall perish, you and all that is yours.'
translations.8: And Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his officials; and he spoke all these words to them; and the men were greatly afraid.
translations.10: And he said to him: 'What did you see, that you did this thing?'
translations.11: Abraham said: 'I said, perhaps there is no fear of God in this place; and they will kill me on account of my wife.
translations.12: And in truth, she is my relative on my father's side, but not on my mother's side; and she became my wife.
translations.13: And when God plucked me from my father's house, I said to her: "This is your kindness which you shall do with me: in every place to which we come, say of me, 'He is my brother.'"
translations.14: And Abimelech took sheep and cattle, male and female slaves, and gave them to Abraham; and he restored to him Sarah his wife.
translations.15: And Abimelech said: 'Behold, my land is before you; wherever is good for you, settle in it.'
translations.16: And to Sarah he said: 'Behold, I have given your brother a thousand drachma; let it be for you as a fine covering for all who are with you; and behold — the whole is before you.'
translations.17: Then Abraham called upon God; and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his maidservants; and they bore [children].
translations.18: For God had threatened to shut up every womb of the house of Abimelech, on account of Sarah, the wife of Abraham.
